evidence.text: The entry analyzes 唱 as 口 plus phonetic 昌 and gives its basic sense as leading a song or musical performance. It quotes the Shuowen gloss 導也 and a Han Feizi passage, 竽唱則諸樂皆和, illustrating the yu leading and the other instruments following. These are dictionary reports and cited texts, not independent proof of when the graph was first written.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「唱」

evidence.text: The entry displays one Small Seal form for 唱 but lists no bronze, oracle-bone, or bamboo/slip forms. This does not establish the date of the graph's origin, nor demonstrate a graphic change or corruption.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「唱」

evidence.text: The entry cites Han Feizi for leading music, Wen Zi for initiating or advocating, Hou Hanshu for praising, Tang Wang Bo and Li He for singing or recitation, Bei Shi for calling out, and Jin Shu for a song or tune as a noun. These citations do not by themselves establish a chronology of semantic changes; the source passages and dated manuscript witnesses were not independently checked here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「唱」

evidence.text: The entry gives Guangyun fanqie 尺亮 and Middle Chinese categories for 唱: initial 昌, departing tone, 宕攝, 陽/漾 rhyme, open division III. These are dictionary categories rather than a direct recording of the sound when the graph was formed.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「唱」

evidence.text: For 昌, the database reports oracle and bronze forms and analyzes the character as 日 plus 口, with a proposed meaning related to calling at sunrise. It also records a scholarly proposal, attributed to Qiu Xigui, that 昌 is an earlier graph for 唱. That proposal concerns a relationship between whole graphs; it is separate from 昌's phonetic role in 唱 and should not be assumed to establish 唱's own earliest form.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「昌」

evidence.text: The 昌 entry gives its Guangyun fanqie as 尺良 and Middle Chinese categories with level tone, while the 唱 entry gives 尺亮 and departing tone. The graph entries thus show related initials and rhyme categories but different tones in Middle Chinese. This comparison supports a phonetic relationship as a traditional analysis; it is not direct evidence of either character's pronunciation at the time of formation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「昌」

evidence.text: The entry identifies 唱 as a phono-semantic compound with semantic 口 and phonetic 昌, and lists Zhengzhang (2003) Old Chinese *tʰjaŋ for 昌 and *tʰjaŋs for 唱. Standard Mandarin is chàng (Pinyin) and Cantonese is coeng3 (Jyutping). The reconstructions are system-specific; the modern readings alone do not establish the ancient phonetic relation.
evidence.title: 唱 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The dossier's reported Baxter-Sagart-derived form /*mə-tʰaŋ-s/ for 唱 differs from Zhengzhang *tʰjaŋs. These reconstructions are not interchangeable; the opened English entry lists Zhengzhang forms, and no primary reconstruction publication was inspected here to adjudicate the difference.
evidence.title: 唱 - 维基词典，自由的多语言词典

evidence.text: The 昌 entry cites oracle-bone use as a ritual name, bronze use with a prosperous/flourishing sense, and bamboo-slip cases where 昌 is read as 唱 or 倡. These graph-borrowing or reading examples concern 昌; they are not attestations of the graph 唱. The database further reports Spring and Autumn/Warring States graphic variants of 昌, including altered placement and shapes of its 日/口 components, and says the Shuowen Small Seal form was misformed relative to an older 曰/口 structure. That account cannot establish a corruption in 唱.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「昌」

evidence.text: The file description identifies 唱-seal.svg as a modern vector depiction of 唱 in Shuowen seal-script style, not a photograph or scan of an ancient artifact. It cites Sinica Database, Chinese Etymology, CUHK's Multi-function Chinese Character Database, and Chinese Text Project as sources, and states a public-domain release for the digital representation. Its individual source image was not visually inspected in this research.
evidence.title: File:唱-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The 昌-seal.svg file description identifies a modern vector depiction in Shuowen seal-script style and names Sinica Database image 27.660C and Chinese Etymology image s04830 as sources. The digital file is marked CC0. It may illustrate the seal-style component graph 昌, but is not an ancient artifact image or a form of 唱.
evidence.title: File:昌-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The 昌 seal file lists versions including oracle, bronze, slip, and silk script, but attempted direct opens of several linked ancient-form pages failed with cache errors. These failed attempts did not establish the exact source images or provenance of any specific earlier-form glyph for use here.
evidence.title: File:昌-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

search_audit.query: Commons links for 昌 seal file versions: Shang oracle, Shang bronze, Western Zhou oracle, Western Zhou bronze, Spring and Autumn bronze, Warring States bronze, Chu slip/silk, Qin slip; opened the Commons file/category links
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the 昌 seal file description and script-category pages. The directly linked individual glyph pages returned cache errors or categories without confirming a character-specific glyph for 昌 beyond the seal file. Earlier-form candidates are therefore not included.

search_audit.query: Open live CUHK 昌 and 唱 dictionary entries to inspect forms, descriptions, and sound categories
search_audit.outcome: Inspected both entries. CUHK displays multiple early script forms for 昌 but only one Small Seal form for 唱; its account of 昌's older forms and readings is explicitly kept separate from the graphic history of 唱.

gaps: No inspected external source established a dated earliest surviving form of the graph 唱, a sequence of its graphic changes, or corruption within 唱. The available CUHK entry displays only a Small Seal 唱 form.

Although CUHK reports early 昌 forms and proposes that 昌 may be the initial graph for the word later written 唱, this is a scholarly proposal about the word/whole graph and does not prove that the written compound 唱 existed in those earlier periods.

The source's citation sequence for senses is not independently checked against primary texts or dated manuscript witnesses. It supports reported uses, not a fully demonstrated chronology or semantic pathway.

Old Chinese forms vary by reconstruction system. Zhengzhang *tʰjaŋ for 昌 and *tʰjaŋs for 唱 provide a plausible phonetic comparison, while the dossier reports an alternative Baxter-Sagart-derived form for 唱. Detailed sound history needs consultation of the underlying reconstruction publications.

No primary reconstruction source was inspected for昌 itself; modern Mandarin readings chāng/chàng and Cantonese readings establish modern contrasts only. This is not a whole-graph phonetic-loan claim, and no object-name borrowing proposal is relevant here.
The proposed Sino-Tibetan comparisons in the dossier remain unverified as cognacy or borrowing claims. No whole-graph borrowing from an external language was established.

The Commons 唱 image is a modern digital redraw. Its file description provides source and reuse assertions, but the page could not be opened in the browser during this turn; visual identity has not been independently inspected.

limitations.text: No artifact photograph or character-specific oracle/bronze/slip image for 唱 was established in this search. The two proposed images are modern vector redrawings in seal-script style. No glyph pixels were visually inspected; captions identify only what the inspected source descriptions claim.
